name: LEO Deorbit Compliance Check (>600km)

actions.description: Violates FCC 5-year post-mission disposal rule without active deorbit
Deployable drag sail or propulsion is required

rationale: At altitudes above 600 km, passive aerodynamic drag is insufficient to deorbit within 5 years.

name: Very Low LEO (<350km) Lifetime Warning

actions.description: Atmospheric drag causes orbital decay within 3-6 months
Station-keeping propulsion needed for sustained operations

rationale: Altitudes below 350 km experience severe atomic oxygen and high atmospheric density.

name: SSO Orbit Configuration for Earth Observation

actions.description: Optimal solar illumination and minimal cloud shadowing
Enables 10-14 passes per day with polar ground stations

rationale: A 10:30 AM or 13:30 PM Sun-Synchronous Orbit maximizes illumination quality for optical imaging.

name: Equatorial Orbit Configuration for Tropical Sensing

actions.description: Concentrates ground tracks between +/-20 degrees latitude
Ground stations near equator provide pass every orbit

rationale: Low inclination orbits provide repeat passes every 90 minutes over tropical latitudes.

name: Van Allen Radiation Belt Edge Warning (>800km)

actions.description: Elevated trapped proton and electron fluxes
Components require >20 krad TID rating and latch-up protection

rationale: Above 800 km altitude, inner Van Allen belt proton flux sharply increases radiation accumulation.

name: Lunar / Deep Space Trajectory Constraints

actions.description: Beyond Earth magnetosphere protection
Severe thermal extremes without Earth IR albedo buffer
Requires DSN 34m/70m dish ground tracking compatibility

rationale: Missions outside Earth orbit lose magnetic field shielding and require deep space communication protocols.

name: Dawn-Dusk SSO Power Advantages

actions.description: Near constant sunlight reduces battery depth-of-discharge cycles
Minimal orbital thermal shock from shadow transitions

rationale: A 06:00/18:00 Dawn-Dusk orbit experiences minimal or zero eclipses for much of the year.

name: VLEO Aerodynamic Feathering

actions.description: Atmospheric torque dominates over solar radiation pressure
Can utilize aerodynamic fins for passive gravity/drag alignment

rationale: In VLEO (250-400 km), atmospheric density creates significant aerodynamic restoring torques.

name: Drag Sail Sizing for Mid-LEO Deorbit

actions.description: Minimum 1.5 m^2 deployable sail ensures compliance with FCC 5-year limit

rationale: A 1.5 m^2 thin-film sail provides sufficient ballistic cross-section for passive decay from 600 km.

name: Propulsion Delta-V for High LEO Deorbit (>650km)

actions.description: Delta-V required to lower perigee into dense atmosphere (<250km)
High total impulse propulsion system necessary

rationale: Above 650 km, drag sails lose effectiveness due to exponential drop in atmospheric density; propulsion is mandatory.

name: Standard Deployer Rail Anodization & Smoothness

actions.description: Rail surface finish must prevent cold welding inside dispenser
Minimum 2 redundant spring-loaded separation kill switches required

rationale: CDS specification requires hard anodized rails and separation switches to keep satellite powered off in canister.

name: Post-Deploy RF Transmitter Silence Period

actions.description: Transmitters and antennas must remain undeployed and inactive for 30 min
Must use hardware watchdog timer independent of flight software

rationale: Launch providers require a 30-minute quiet period after dispenser ejection before any antenna deployment or RF broadcast.

name: Launch Structural Fundamental Frequency Limit

actions.description: First natural resonant mode must exceed 90 Hz to avoid dispenser coupling
Internal stiffening ribs required across long structural panels

rationale: Large CubeSats suffer from low-frequency structural deflection under launch acoustic and vibration loads.

name: Pressurized Propulsion Leakage Safety Inhibits

actions.description: 3 independent physical inhibits required to prevent propellant release prior to deployment
Pressure vessel burst qualification factor of 2.0x working pressure

rationale: Rideshare safety regulations demand fail-safe triple inhibits on any pressurized fluid/gas system.

name: Non-Toxic Green Monopropellant Mandate

actions.description: Hydrazine strictly prohibited on rideshare; use LMP-103S or AF-M315E/ASCENT
Permits fueling at standard integration facilities

rationale: Secondary rideshare CubeSats are not permitted to use hypergolic or toxic hydrazine due to personnel hazard.

name: SAR Payload Form Factor Requirement

actions.description: SAR antenna feeds and power converters require at least 6U, preferably 12U
Minimizes thermal distortion on radar phase array

rationale: Synthetic Aperture Radar payloads cannot fit mechanically or thermally into form factors smaller than 6U.

name: Hyperspectral Imager Volume Constraint

actions.description: Offner/Dyson spectrometer optics need >2U of dedicated internal optical path
Leaves 3U for payload and 3U for bus, battery, and ADCS

rationale: Hyperspectral spectrometers require dedicated folded focal lengths and slit assemblies requiring at least 2-3U.

name: Earth Observation Optical Camera Form Factor

actions.description: Telescope aperture (>= 70-90mm) requires at least 1.5U optical volume
Standard 3U configuration provides balance for optics and downlink

rationale: Sub-5m GSD optical cameras require telescope focal length that exceeds single 1U boundaries.

name: IoT / AIS Receiver Form Factor Compatibility

actions.description: RF receiver payload can be accommodated in 0.5U within a 1U-3U bus
2U allows ample deployable tape-spring dipole antennas

rationale: SDR-based IoT and maritime AIS payloads have low mass and volume envelopes feasible in compact CubeSats.

name: Biological / Microfluidics Payload Lab Volume

actions.description: Requires fluid reservoir, incubation chamber, and optical density reader
Permits thermal insulation barrier around biological specimens

rationale: Life science payloads require pressurized fluid containment and autonomous incubator chambers.

name: Deep Space 12U/16U Architecture Mandate

actions.description: Deep space missions require delta-V propulsion, high-gain X/Ka antenna, and deep radiation shielding
Optimal standard for lunar flyby / orbital CubeSat architectures

rationale: Interplanetary CubeSats (like MarCO, CAPSTONE) require 6U-12U minimum to carry propulsion and Iris deep space radios.

name: Total Mass Budget Validation for 1U

actions.description: CalPoly CubeSat Design Spec 1U maximum mass constraint
Allocated mass limit for payload instrument

rationale: Standard 1U CubeSats cannot exceed 1.33 kg to be compliant with P-POD deployers.

name: Total Mass Budget Validation for 2U

actions.description: CalPoly CubeSat Design Spec 2U maximum mass constraint
Allocated mass limit for payload instrument

rationale: Standard 2U CubeSats cannot exceed 2.66 kg total mass.

name: Total Mass Budget Validation for 3U

actions.description: CalPoly CubeSat Design Spec 3U maximum mass constraint
Allocated mass limit for payload instrument

rationale: Standard 3U CubeSats cannot exceed 4.0 kg total mass.

name: Total Mass Budget Validation for 6U

actions.description: Standard canister dispenser 6U mass limit (up to 12kg)
Allocated mass limit for payload instrument

rationale: Standard 6U CubeSats allow up to 12.0 kg total mass.

name: Total Mass Budget Validation for 12U

actions.description: Standard 12U dispenser mass limit (up to 24kg)
Allocated mass limit for payload instrument

rationale: Standard 12U CubeSats allow up to 24.0 kg total mass.

name: Center of Mass Envelope Offset Check

actions.description: Center of gravity must lie within 20mm of geometric center

rationale: CDS specification requires CG within tight tolerance to prevent jamming in deployer guide rails.

name: Modular PC/104 Stack vs Backplane Architecture

actions.description: Replace PC/104 stack with rigid backplane harness to save volume and increase reliability

rationale: Larger CubeSats (6U+) benefit from backplane topologies rather than stacking connectors.

name: External Component Protrusion Constraint

actions.description: No component may extend beyond 6.5mm from exterior face before release

rationale: Dispenser rails have strict keep-out envelopes to avoid catching on canister walls during spring release.

name: Solar Array Hinged Latch Redundancy

actions.description: Use redundant burn wires (Nichrome or Vectran tie) for release activation

rationale: Single-point deployable solar panel failures are a leading cause of CubeSat mission loss.

name: High Power Payload Demands Deployable Solar Panels

actions.description: Body-mounted panels cannot satisfy >25W continuous orbit-average power
Single-axis solar array drive assembly recommended

rationale: Peak loads exceeding 25W exceed body-mounted solar generation capabilities in standard CubeSat sizes.

name: Low Power IoT Body Mounted Panels Sufficient

actions.description: Body-mounted panels eliminate deployment risk for low-power mission

rationale: Power draws under 3W are easily sustained by body-mounted triple-junction solar cells.

name: Battery Capacity Sizing for Eclipse Duration

actions.description: Wh = (P_avg * 0.65 hr) / (DoD_max * 0.90)

rationale: Battery must sustain full satellite power draw during 35-40 minutes of eclipse with safe depth-of-discharge.

name: Battery Chemistry Selection: LEO Cycling Life

actions.description: 18650 cylindrical cells with strict 20-30% DoD provide >16,000 cycles
Active thermal control needed to keep battery > 5C

rationale: Pouch cells degrade quickly in long LEO missions due to thermal gradient stress and high cycle count.

name: High Bus Voltage (28V) for High Power Systems

actions.description: Higher bus voltage minimizes I^2*R copper ohmic losses across wiring harness
Maximum Power Point Tracking buck-boost regulator

rationale: At loads >60W, standard 3.3V/5V/12V distribution causes unacceptable current levels and thermal dissipation.

name: Standard Bus Voltage (5V / 12V) for 3U Subsystems

actions.description: Dual rail accommodates ADCS reaction wheels (12V) and avionics (5V/3.3V)

rationale: Standard CubeSat subsystems primarily interface via regulated 5V and 12V power rails.

name: Low Power Single Bus Architecture (3.3V/5V)

actions.description: High-efficiency synchronous buck converters for microcontroller avionics

rationale: Simpler dual low-voltage rails maximize converter efficiency for sub-15W satellites.

name: Deep Space Solar Cell Area Margin (1 AU to 1.5 AU)

actions.description: Solar flux drops with inverse-square law; at Mars (1.52 AU) flux is 44% of Earth
Array area must be oversized by 2.3x compared to 1 AU LEO equivalent

rationale: Interplanetary missions moving away from the Sun must oversize solar arrays to compensate for flux falloff.

name: Triple Junction Solar Cell Selection

actions.description: State-of-the-art space flight qualified 29.5-30% efficiency cells

rationale: Silicon solar cells are obsolete for CubeSats due to strict volume and surface area constraints.

name: Overcurrent Protection and Latch-up Current Limiting

actions.description: Sub-millisecond hardware cutoffs for Single Event Latch-ups (SEL)
Payload power isolated from primary bus flight computer

rationale: Radiation-induced single-event latchups will destroy CMOS components without fast current limiting.

name: Battery Cold Environment Heater Control

actions.description: Dedicated heater budget to keep battery temperature above 0C during eclipse
Bimetallic strip or thermistor control independent of software

rationale: Charging Li-ion batteries below 0 deg C causes permanent lithium dendrite plating and catastrophic short circuits.

name: Deployable Solar Array Sun-Tracking SADA

actions.description: Increases daily power harvest by 35-45% without off-pointing payload

rationale: High power payloads (SAR, radar) require sun-tracking solar arrays so the spacecraft can maintain nadir pointing.

name: Peak Shaving Battery Sizing for High RF Transmit

actions.description: Ensures battery discharge rate does not exceed 1C continuous rating
Parallel supercapacitor bank absorbs transmit surge current

rationale: High power transmitters (X-band, Ka-band) pulse 20-40W of RF power during ground station passes.

name: EPS Energy Balance Margin Rule

actions.description: Orbit-average power generated must exceed average consumption by at least 30%

rationale: NASA standard requires at least 30% margin between orbit-average power generation and satellite consumption.

name: Solar Cell Radiation Degradation Sizing Factor

actions.description: Derate solar cell capacity by 15-20% for End-of-Life (EOL) calculation

rationale: Radiation, micrometeroid pitting, and thermal cycling degrade solar cell output by ~2.5% per year in LEO.

name: High Volume Payload Downlink: X-Band Requirement

actions.description: Data volume >= 10 GB/day requires high-rate X-band downlink (20-100 Mbps)
Requires directional patch antenna or phased array
Requires 3-axis pointing toward ground station during pass

rationale: Downlinking gigabytes of optical or SAR data during brief 8-minute passes requires X-band or Ka-band rates.

name: Ultra High Volume Payload Downlink: Optical Laser Comm

actions.description: Data volumes > 100 GB/day require optical laser communication terminal
Requires ultra-fine star-tracker pointing and fast-steering mirror

rationale: Extremely high data rates (1+ Gbps) demand optical communication to avoid spectrum licensing choke points.

name: Medium Data Volume: S-Band Downlink

actions.description: S-Band provides 1-5 Mbps downlink, sufficient for 0.5-10 GB daily data
Compact body-mounted patch antenna

rationale: S-Band is the ideal industry workhorse for medium-throughput CubeSat data downlinks.

name: Low Data Rate IoT: UHF Downlink Sufficient

actions.description: UHF (435-438 MHz) provides 9.6-19.2 kbps, ideal for IoT, telemetry & science housekeeping
Omnidirectional pattern eliminates strict pointing requirements during downlink

rationale: Low data volume missions benefit from omnidirectional UHF coverage and simple ground station hardware.

name: Amateur vs Commercial Frequency Licensing

actions.description: Commercial entities cannot use amateur UHF/VHF bands; must file commercial space spectrum with FCC/ITU
Requires 12-18 months advance coordination

rationale: IARU amateur satellite frequencies are strictly reserved for non-profit education and experimental radio hobbyists.

name: Deep Space Iris Radio for Lunar / Interplanetary

actions.description: Deep Space Network (DSN) compatible X-band transponder
High gain antenna (>26 dBi) required to close link over lunar/planetary distance

rationale: Communications beyond Earth orbit require specialized transponders supporting coherent ranging and DSN protocols.

name: Dual Redundant Telemetry & Telecommand (TT&C)

actions.description: Independent UHF/VHF receiver ensures command access even if satellite loses attitude orientation

rationale: Never rely exclusively on high-gain directional antennas for telemetry and emergency command recovery.

name: Link Margin Safety Buffer Standard

actions.description: Minimum 3 dB positive link margin required under worst-case 5-degree ground station elevation

rationale: NASA / DoD communications design guidelines require at least 3 dB link margin to absorb atmospheric attenuation.

name: Rain Attenuation Margin for Ka-Band

actions.description: Ka-band signals suffer severe rain fade; ground stations require site diversity

rationale: Ka-band frequencies (26-40 GHz) experience up to 10 dB attenuation through rain and heavy cloud moisture.

name: Inter-Satellite Link (ISL) for Real-Time Constellation Access

actions.description: Relay patch antenna sends critical alerts to LEO constellation with < 10 second latency

rationale: Using Iridium Short Burst Data or Globalstar allows immediate anomaly reporting without waiting for ground pass.

name: Sub-0.1 Degree Pointing Demands Star Tracker & Reaction Wheels

actions.description: Reaction wheels provide precision torque and fine attitude agility
Star tracker delivers arcsecond attitude determination
Magnetic torque coils desaturate wheel angular momentum

rationale: High resolution optical imaging and inter-satellite pointing cannot be achieved with sun sensors alone.

name: Moderate Pointing (1 to 5 Degrees): Magnetorquers & Coarse Sun Sensors

actions.description: Magnetic rods provide reliable 3-axis damping and coarse orientation
Economical sensor suite sufficient for coarse Earth/Sun orientation

rationale: Coarse pointing payloads (e.g. wide-angle cameras, radio beacons) do not require costly reaction wheels.

name: Passive Magnetic Damping for Simple IoT / Telemetry

actions.description: Aligns spacecraft along Earth magnetic field vector with zero power consumption
Zero electrical power drawn by ADCS

rationale: Passive magnetic stabilization is essentially failure-proof and draws zero watts of power.

name: Magnetorquer Ineffectiveness in Deep Space

actions.description: Planetary/interplanetary magnetic field is negligible (~0 nT)
Requires reaction control thrusters (RCS) for wheel momentum dump

rationale: Outside Earth's magnetosphere, magnetorquers cannot produce control torque.

name: Jitter Isolation for High-Res Imagery

actions.description: Isolates wheel high-frequency harmonic vibrations from optical payload

rationale: Reaction wheel imbalance causes micro-vibrations (jitter) that blur optical ground images.

name: B-Dot Rate Damping Algorithm for Post-Deploy Detumble

actions.description: Damps high tip-off angular rates (< 30 deg/sec) down to < 2 deg/sec within 2 orbits

rationale: The B-dot control law using magnetorquers is the universal standard for CubeSat post-separation detumbling.

name: GPS / GNSS Receiver Requirement for Autonomous Orbit Determination

actions.description: Provides real-time position, velocity, and nanosecond PPS timing to payload and ADCS
Real-time propagation for nadir and target-tracking pointing

rationale: Precision payloads require knowing accurate spacecraft position for ground target pointing.

name: High Power Dissipation Demands Dedicated Thermal Radiator

actions.description: High emissivity radiator panel positioned on anti-sun face
Transfers concentrated payload amplifier heat to outer radiator panel

rationale: CubeSats dissipating >30W will overheat internal avionics without dedicated radiators and heat transport.

name: Optical Telescope Athermalization

actions.description: Near-zero coefficient of thermal expansion prevents thermal defocusing
10-layer aluminized Mylar MLI isolates optical bay from bus fluctuations

rationale: Thermal expansion of aluminum barrel causes defocusing and image degradation across orbital thermal cycles.

name: Battery Thermal Enclosure Isolation

actions.description: Conductively isolates battery pack from cold outer aluminum chassis
Engages heaters when battery core temp drops below +2C

rationale: Batteries have the narrowest allowable operating temperature range (0 to 35C) of any CubeSat component.

name: Cryocooler Integration for Thermal Infrared (TIR) Payload

actions.description: Cools LWIR sensor focal plane down to 80K (-193C) to reduce dark current noise
Requires 15-25W continuous power allocation for cryocooler compressor

rationale: Long-wave infrared focal plane arrays must be cryogenically cooled to achieve useful radiometric signal.

name: Passive Thermal Control for Low Power Small CubeSat

actions.description: Balanced surface emissivity/absorptivity ratios maintain equilibrium at 10-30C

rationale: Sub-15W CubeSats generally maintain equilibrium without active radiators through careful passive finish selection.

name: Constellation Orbit Phasing: Electrospray / Ion Propulsion

actions.description: High specific impulse (Isp > 800s) provides >150 m/s delta-V for constellation slot insertion
Fits within standard 1U modular propulsion bay

rationale: High Isp electric propulsion is ideal for constellation altitude raising, slot phasing, and lifetime drag makeup.

name: Rapid Slew / High Impulse Maneuver: Chemical Green Monoprop

actions.description: Provides high thrust (0.5 - 1.0 N) required for rapid impulsive rendezvous maneuvers

rationale: Electric propulsion thrust (0.1-5 mN) is far too slow for time-critical orbital proximity operations.

name: Zero Toxicity Cold Gas for Educational 3U/6U

actions.description: Inert propellant with zero toxic handling or thermal ignition hazards; simplest range safety approval

rationale: University teams face extreme regulatory hurdles with toxic or reactive propellants; cold gas is safest.

name: Deep Space Lunar Insertion Delta-V Requirement

actions.description: Requires >= 450 m/s delta-V for Lunar Orbit Insertion (LOI) or weak stability boundary capture
High density total impulse required

rationale: Entering lunar orbit from translunar injection demands substantial delta-V.

name: Payload-Power Compatibility Inconsistency Check

actions.description: Physical conflict: 1U-2U form factor cannot generate or dissipate 50W of power
Must increase spacecraft size to at least 6U

rationale: Violates physical conservation of surface area for solar collection and thermal rejection.

name: Payload Data Volume vs UHF Communication Mismatch

actions.description: UHF link (9.6 kbps) would take > 50 days to download 1 day of data
Forced upgrade to X-band downlink to prevent memory buffer overflow

rationale: Data throughput mismatch: UHF link cannot service megabyte/gigabyte payload production rates.

name: Optical Instrument ADCS Stability Requirement Check

actions.description: Pointing error > 1 deg causes severe ground target miss and motion blur
Tightened pointing tolerance to 0.1 deg

rationale: Optical imaging from 500km altitude requires sub-0.1 degree stabilization during ground exposures.

name: Deep Space Ground Station Incompatibility Alert

actions.description: Standard amateur or commercial LEO ground stations have insufficient G/T to receive beyond LEO
Forced switch to NASA Deep Space Network or ESA Estrack 35m stations

rationale: Inverse square free-space path loss to the Moon (>384,000 km) cannot close with standard 3m dishes.

name: Mass Margin Compliance Check

actions.description: Ensures (M_max - M_dry) / M_max >= 20%

rationale: AIAA S-120 and NASA standard require 20% dry mass margin at Preliminary Design Review.

name: Fault-Tolerant OBC Architecture for High Radiation

actions.description: TMR architecture with voting logic mitigates single event upsets (SEUs)
Ferroelectric RAM resists radiation corruption better than standard Flash/SRAM

rationale: In high radiation zones, software SEUs will corrupt flight computer memory without hardware/software TMR.

name: COTS Microcontroller Architecture for Short LEO Mission

actions.description: Cost-effective ARM Cortex-M4 flight computer with external watchdog supervisor

rationale: Short duration low-altitude university CubeSats can rely on COTS microcontrollers protected by watchdogs.

name: High Current Wiring Harness Safety Sizing

actions.description: Prevents resistive thermal buildup in vacuum environment

rationale: Vacuum prevents convective cooling; undersized wires will overheat and melt insulation.

name: Autonomous Hard Reset Hardware Watchdog

actions.description: Autonomous full EPS power-cycle reboot every 24 hours if heartbeat lost

rationale: Loss of contact from frozen flight computers is recovered by hardware-timed power cycle resets.

name: Comprehensive CubeSat Configuration Feasibility Signoff

actions.description: Spacecraft configuration complies with mass, power, communication, and orbital disposal standards

rationale: Synthesizes subsystem assessments to produce formal mission viability rating.

name: Earth Observation RGB Ground Resolution Rule

actions.description: Achievable Ground Sampling Distance <= 3 meters
Allocated camera sensor mass

rationale: Sub-500km altitude allows aperture to achieve 3m GSD in optical spectrum.

name: Earth Observation High Altitude GSD Degradation

actions.description: Achievable Ground Sampling Distance degrades to 7-8 meters due to optical diffraction

rationale: Diffraction limits GSD proportionally to orbital altitude for a given optical aperture.

name: Hyperspectral Data Volume Calculation

actions.description: 128 contiguous spectral bands across VNIR/SWIR
Generates 80 GB per operational day requiring high-speed onboard compression

rationale: Hyperspectral data cubes generate immense raw data volumes per square kilometer.

name: SAR Pulse Repetition Frequency Power Draw

actions.description: Radar transmitter draws high peak power during active swath pass
Operates at max 5% duty cycle to manage thermal dissipation
Daily radar raw data acquisition volume

rationale: Active microwave radar requires substantial RF transmit power, limited to short bursts.

name: Maritime AIS Receiver Antenna Selection

actions.description: Tuned to marine VHF frequencies 161.975 MHz and 162.025 MHz
Downlinks 300 MB of processed ship position reports

rationale: Maritime AIS operates in marine VHF band requiring dedicated quarter-wave antennas.

name: Space Weather Dosimeter Low Resource Allocation

actions.description: Low power consumption enables continuous operation across all orbits
Low data telemetry volume

rationale: Solid state silicon dosimeters have minimal power and volume footprints.

name: Atmospheric Langmuir Probe Boom Deployment

actions.description: Deployable boom required to place sensor outside spacecraft plasma sheath and charging wake

rationale: Langmuir probes measure ionospheric plasma density and must avoid satellite chassis contamination.

name: Gamma-Ray Burst Scintillator Shielding

actions.description: Suppresses background cosmic radiation and secondary gamma rays

rationale: High-energy astrophysics detectors require passive graded shielding to achieve high signal-to-noise.

name: Thermal IR Detector Vacuum Enclosure

actions.description: Isolates detector focal plane array from surrounding chassis radiative heat

rationale: Cryocooled IR sensors need vacuum dewar enclosures to prevent parasitic heat conduction.

name: Optical Payload Sun-Blind Protection Shutter

actions.description: Prevents direct solar burn-in on CMOS sensor during off-nominal tumbling

rationale: Accidental sun pointing during tumble will permanently destroy unshielded focal plane arrays.

name: Reaction Wheel Sizing for 6U Platform

actions.description: 0.05 Nms momentum storage accommodates orbital gravity gradient and magnetic torques

rationale: 6U satellites have typical moment of inertia requiring 0.02-0.05 Nms storage wheels.

name: Reaction Wheel Sizing for 12U/16U Platform

actions.description: 0.20 Nms momentum storage wheels prevent premature saturation

rationale: Higher moments of inertia in 12U/16U platforms require wheels with larger angular momentum capacity.

name: Star Tracker Boresight Redundancy

actions.description: Dual optical heads prevent attitude blind spots when Earth or Sun occludes one camera

rationale: Single star trackers lose attitude lock when the Earth limb or Sun enters their field of view.

name: Magnetometer Deployment on Non-Magnetic Boom

actions.description: Separates magnetometer from internal bus magnetic fields generated by batteries and solar panel currents

rationale: Internal satellite current loops produce parasitic magnetic fields that corrupt magnetometer measurements.

name: Sun Sensor Glint Rejection Filtering

actions.description: Algorithms filter out Earth albedo reflections that spoof sun vector

rationale: Earth albedo reflection in LEO can confuse coarse photodiode sun sensors.

name: Target Tracking Slew Rate Requirement

actions.description: Slew rate >= 2.5 deg/sec required to maintain camera pointing on ground target during overflight

rationale: Spotlight ground target imaging requires pitching backwards at up to 2-3 deg/sec to cancel orbital ground motion.

name: Magnetic Torquer Sizing for High Altitude Desaturation

actions.description: Geomagnetic field decreases as 1/r^3; torque rods must be upsized by 50%

rationale: Earth's B-field weakens significantly at higher LEO altitudes, reducing desaturation torque.

name: UHF Link Budget Margin Check

actions.description: Generous 12 dB link margin with 14 dBi Yagi ground station

rationale: UHF paths have low free-space path loss ensuring reliable communications even in degraded attitudes.

name: S-Band Transmit Power Amplification

actions.description: 2W RF power output achieves 2 Mbps downlink to 3m dish

rationale: 2W S-band transmitter provides robust link across 2000 km slant ranges.

name: X-Band Phased Array Beam Steering

actions.description: Electronic beam steering steers RF link without rolling the entire spacecraft

rationale: AESA phased arrays permit high gain downlink while spacecraft keeps payload pointing nadir.

name: DVB-S2 Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM)

actions.description: Dynamically adjusts modulation (QPSK to 32APSK) based on ground station elevation angle

rationale: DVB-S2 ACM increases pass data throughput by 80-120% over fixed modulation schemes.

name: Ground Station Contact Elevation Angle Cutoff

actions.description: Horizon cutoff set at 5 deg to prevent tropospheric multi-path and terrain blockage

rationale: Below 5 degrees elevation, tropospheric scintillation and thermal noise severely degrade link performance.

name: Peak Power Battery Discharging Temperature Derating

actions.description: High continuous discharge elevates internal battery cell temperature

rationale: Internal resistance I^2*R causes battery self-heating during high power discharges.

name: Solar Array Shadowing Bypass Diodes

actions.description: Prevents hot-spot destructive reverse breakdown if panel is partially shadowed by antenna/booms

rationale: Partial shadowing of a single solar cell forces it to dissipate reverse power, risking fire or burnout.

name: CubeSat Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT)

actions.description: Increases energy harvest by 20-30% across wide solar cell thermal swings

rationale: Direct energy transfer loses energy as solar cell V_mp shifts drastically between -100C and +100C.

name: Payload Focal Plane Thermal Dissipation Path

actions.description: Conducts heat from sensor focal plane to satellite chassis radiator

rationale: CMOS sensors generate heat that degrades dark current noise if not sinked to the outer structure.

name: Battery Thermal Enclosure Multi-Layer Insulation

actions.description: Reduces heater energy demand by 60% during long winter eclipses

rationale: Thermal insulation around battery box conserves precious battery power in eclipse.

name: Anodized Aluminum 6061-T6 Chassis Specification

actions.description: Space flight heritage alloy offering optimal strength-to-weight and thermal conductivity

rationale: 6061-T6 is standard flight proven material for CubeSat primary load-bearing chassis.

name: Outgassing Material Selection Standard (CVCM & TML)

actions.description: Prevents volatile condensable organic deposition on telescope lenses and mirrors

rationale: Condensable outgassed materials in vacuum permanently coat optical surfaces.

name: Autonomous Safe Hold Mode Definition

actions.description: Orients solar arrays directly at Sun, turns off payload, activates low-rate beacon

rationale: Autonomous safe hold protects satellite from power depletion upon software or hardware anomalies.

name: Total System Power Margin Signoff

actions.description: Calculated power generation exceeds maximum operating profile with >25% margin

rationale: Ensures satellite meets AIAA / NASA design margin requirements for Preliminary Design Review.
